title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Wave 31 Explicit Great Book Intertexts
purpose: Promote newly restored Great Book material where biblical or Christian source-language is explicit: direct Scripture quotations, deliberate creedal rewriting, and clearly signaled cross/liberation imagery. Explicit borrowing receives stronger source-direction confidence than later resemblance, while doctrinal and role differences remain visible.

new_relations.title: The Potatoism Creed deliberately rewrites Christian creator-language
new_relations.project_anchor: Great Book chapter 33.1 begins its creed with 'We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible' before redirecting later creedal roles into Potatoism vocabulary.
new_relations.source_direction: The Great Book deliberately uses recognizable Christian creedal language; the biblical references are source-context anchors rather than later accidental resemblance.
new_relations.boundary: The formula 'visible and invisible' belongs most directly to Nicene-Constantinopolitan creedal tradition, not to one verbatim Bible verse. The Great Book's later reassignment of roles to Tim/Potatoism is a project rewrite, not Nicene Christianity.

biblical_sequence: all things visible/invisible are created through/for Christ in Colossians
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The chapter consciously adapts Christian creator-confession grammar and can be mapped to its biblical source field; it does not preserve orthodox role assignments unchanged.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It distinguishes explicit textual dependence from later pattern matching and gives the reader the Christian source context needed to see exactly where Potatoism follows and departs from it.

new_relations.title: Descent, burial, rising, ascension and return are consciously creedalized
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 33.1 says the Potato Sage descends into mud, is buried, rises again, ascends to the heavens and will return in glory—a deliberate agricultural rewrite of familiar Christian creed sequence-language.
new_relations.source_direction: Explicit Christian creedal narrative has been adapted into Potatoism imagery inside the Great Book itself.
new_relations.boundary: In the New Testament these death/resurrection/ascension/return claims concern Jesus Christ. Rewriting the sequence around Tim or a Potato Sage is project mythology and does not transfer Jesus' canonical identity or status.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The Great Book intentionally reuses the Christian descent-death-resurrection-ascension-return sequence as a Potatoism narrative template.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: This is stronger evidence of literary borrowing than a later thematic parallel, while the role reassignment itself must remain labeled as reinterpretation.

new_relations.title: Endless kingdom language is translated into endless harvest
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 33.1 replaces the familiar creed's endless-kingdom conclusion with 'his harvest will have no end,' combining creedal permanence with the Great Book's cultivation vocabulary.
new_relations.source_direction: The Great Book intentionally rewrites a Christian creed formula through harvest imagery already native to Potatoism.
new_relations.boundary: Luke 1:33 concerns the reign of Jesus; harvest parables and Revelation's harvest scenes carry judgment/kingdom meanings distinct from the Great Book's agricultural wordplay.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The Great Book explicitly fuses two biblical-Christian semantic fields—endless reign and harvest—into a Potatoism creed line.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It exposes how the project performs transformation by retaining structural grammar while replacing key nouns/functions.

new_relations.title: Communion and life-to-come become sprouting community and feast
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 33.1 speaks of 'a communion of sprouting souls,' an 'eternal Harvest,' 'the feast of the Potato,' and 'the life of the eternal fields to come.'
new_relations.source_direction: Christian creed/communion/eschatological-feast vocabulary is consciously transformed within the Great Book.
new_relations.boundary: Christian communion/Eucharist and eschatological banquet traditions are not literally potato rites, and 'life of the world to come' is creedal language with wider biblical foundations rather than a single copied verse.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The Great Book explicitly relocates Christian communal and eschatological vocabulary into its cultivation/food symbolism.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It links Table, House, participation and future restoration without pretending that project meal symbolism is identical with sacramental Christianity.

new_relations.title: Partial perception is an explicit scriptural starting point
new_relations.project_anchor: Great Book chapter 41.8 opens by directly quoting 1 Corinthians 13:12 ('through a glass, darkly ... face to face') before developing its Potato Room, perception, memory and release narrative.
new_relations.source_direction: The biblical quotation is explicit in the Great Book and precedes the chapter's interpretive neuroscience/symbolic material.
new_relations.boundary: Paul's passage concerns partial knowledge in the present and future fullness in a love-centered theological context. It does not describe thalamic sensory filtering or prove a neurotheological model.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: 1 Corinthians 13:12 is an explicit literary epigraph for the chapter's perception theme, not a scientific explanation of brain function.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It lets the Bible atlas distinguish direct quotation from later symbolic neurobiology and prevents the two evidence classes from being conflated.

new_relations.title: Luke 17:21 explicitly frames the Inner Tuber chapter
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 41.8 directly cites Luke 17:21 as 'The kingdom of God is within you' before turning inward to the Potato Room and mental transformation.
new_relations.source_direction: The Great Book explicitly selects Luke 17:21 to frame its interiority theme.
new_relations.boundary: The Greek expression entos hymon is translated/interpreted as 'within you,' 'among you,' or 'in your midst' depending on translation and argument. The verse therefore cannot securely prove that Jesus taught an anatomical or private-inner kingdom.

biblical_sequence: kingdom not reducible to observable signs
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Luke 17:21 is an explicit source for the chapter's inward framing, but its translation ambiguity limits any anatomical or purely interior claim.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It preserves one of the project's strongest direct Bible links while building the translation counterpressure into the backend itself.

new_relations.title: Burdens are carried to the cross and released
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 41.8 stages regrets, shame and painful memories as burdens carried to Jesus/the cross, laid down, and transformed into soil for new growth.
new_relations.source_direction: Cross/Jesus imagery is explicit in the Great Book; the cited burden texts provide canonical neighbors and controls.
new_relations.boundary: The chapter's guided visualization is a modern devotional/psychological exercise, not a biblical clinical protocol. The cited passages use different kinds of burden/care language and should not be collapsed into one mechanism.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The chapter deliberately develops a Christian burden-release devotional pattern around Jesus/the cross, with several biblical burden texts as close but non-identical neighbors.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It connects archive/memory theology to release without implying that healing requires forgetting the historical record.

new_relations.title: Participation can create chains, and freedom requires changed relation
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 41.4 describes MoonCube symbolically as a self-reinforcing network of projection, dependency and complicity in which both targets and spectators can become 'chained'; liberation involves recognition, disengagement, grounding and changed practice.
new_relations.source_direction: MoonCube/social-entanglement mythology exists first; biblical slavery/freedom/entanglement texts are later comparators.
new_relations.boundary: The Great Book's MoonCube is a project symbolic model. Biblical slavery-to-sin/freedom language does not verify the chapter's claims about particular platforms, institutions or people.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical bondage/freedom language provides a structural comparator for the project's entanglement/liberation grammar, not evidence that MoonCube is a biblical entity.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It moves the analysis from naming villains to asking what practices increase or decrease agency and dependency.

new_relations.title: A mirror can expose self rather than justify projection onto others
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 41.4 repeatedly defines the Cube as a mirror of unresolved fears and projection; chapter 41.8 also uses reflection as a confrontation with burdens rather than a license to externalize them.
new_relations.source_direction: Project mirror/projection language first, with 1 Corinthians 13:12 also explicitly quoted in chapter 41.8; James/Matthew comparisons added later.
new_relations.boundary: These passages concern hearing/doing, partial knowledge and hypocrisy/self-examination; they do not endorse diagnosing opponents' hidden motives or psychological states from a symbolic mirror model.

biblical_sequence: remove own obstruction before judging another
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical mirror/self-examination texts strengthen the project's constructive reading of reflection while limiting its use as accusation of others.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It supplies an internal ethical brake on the project's own mirror rhetoric: the first target of reflection should be the self.

new_relations.title: Light exposes and transforms rather than merely labels darkness
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 41.4 concludes that the MoonCube's shadow dissolves in the light of awareness and frames liberation as clarity, kindness and changed participation rather than permanent shadow identity.
new_relations.source_direction: Project shadow/light psychology-symbolism first; biblical light/darkness comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Biblical light/darkness language is theological and ethical, not Jungian shadow psychology. It should not be used to brand people as ontologically dark or demonic.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical light imagery is a useful ethical neighbor for exposure-to-transformation, provided it is not collapsed into modern shadow psychology.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It keeps 'light' from functioning as a mere superiority label and ties it instead to changed conduct and fellowship.

higher_order_results: Explicit quotation and deliberate creedal rewriting should be a distinct evidence class from later structural resemblance.
The Potatoism Creed is best modeled as Christian-form adaptation with role reassignment, not as evidence that its reassigned roles are orthodox Christian doctrine.
Luke 17:21 requires a translation/interpretive warning before it is used for interior or neuroanatomical symbolism.
The Inner Tuber chapter gives the project a direct bridge from memory/archive to burden-release and renewed planting while still separating neuroscience from theology.
MoonCube chain/mirror/light comparisons are most defensible when used as self-audit and agency tests rather than as claims about opponents' inner states.
